questions.stem: Where do white dwarfs sit on the HR diagram?

options.explanation: Top left holds the brightest hot main sequence stars.

options.explanation: Cool (red) and luminous (giant size) — top right.
Hot but dim.

questions.stem: State the two quantities an HR diagram plots.
questions.modelAnswer: Luminosity on the y-axis and surface temperature on the x-axis.

questions.stem: State where most stars are found on the HR diagram.
questions.modelAnswer: Most stars lie on the main sequence, the band from top left to bottom right.

questions.stem: Explain why the main sequence band runs from top left to bottom right.
questions.modelAnswer: Main sequence stars trade temperature against luminosity: the hottest ones are also the brightest, so they sit top-left, while cooler, dimmer ones extend the band down to the bottom right.

questions.stem: A star is plotted with temperature 20,000 K and luminosity 10,000 times the Sun's. Locate its region.
questions.modelAnswer: 20,000 K sits far left (hot) and a luminosity of 10⁴ sits high up (bright), so the star lands on the upper main sequence among the large hot stars.

questions.stem: A star with luminosity 100 times the Sun's is plotted at…

options.explanation: That is a hundredth, the wrong direction.
Solar units scale directly from the Sun's value of 1.
That is the Sun itself.
That is 10 000 times, not 100 times.

questions.stem: The Sun's own luminosity on the HR diagram is…

options.explanation: That is a far brighter star.
The scale is defined by the Sun.
Solar units take the Sun as the unit.
The Sun shines; its value is not zero.

questions.stem: To plot a star at 20 000 K, you locate that temperature…

options.explanation: The right end is coolest.

options.text: halfway only if the star is red
options.explanation: Colour does not move the position.

options.text: towards the left side of the reversed temperature axis
options.explanation: Hotter sits further left.

options.text: bottom left with the white dwarfs
options.explanation: X is far too luminous for that region.

questions.stem: State the luminosity value used for the Sun on the HR diagram.
questions.modelAnswer: The Sun's luminosity is 1 in solar units.

questions.stem: State the luminosity coordinate of a star 10 000 times the Sun's.
Explain how the reversed temperature axis changes where hot stars are plotted.
questions.modelAnswer: Because temperature runs backwards, the hottest stars land on the left of the diagram, so a hot bright star such as one at 20 000 K plots towards the top left, not the top right.

questions.stem: Plot Star X: surface temperature 20 000 K, luminosity 10 000 times the Sun. Give the coordinates.
questions.modelAnswer: Temperature coordinate 20 000 K on the reversed axis; luminosity coordinate 10⁴ solar units (10 000 × 1); mark and label the point.
